public_title: Why Your Jaw Drops on News 🤐
hook: You drop your jaw when you hear big news.

sections.title: Story
sections.narration: You drop your jaw when you hear big news. That movement is actually a threat signal. In 1999, Ekman filmed this reaction, noting about 0.5 seconds of tension. The result? Your body prepares to flee. Research shows the jaw drops to widen the airway. That helps you breathe deeply. It is a survival tool. Does it still hold today? Yes. Modern scans show the same muscle activation. It is not just a habit. It is a reflex. So why do we assume it is just shock? Because we ignore the body response. The reflex primes you for action. It is not about the face. It is about the lungs. You need oxygen to fight or run. That is why the jaw drops. So next time you hear unexpected news, remember your jaw drops. You drop your jaw when you hear big news.

claims.claim: Facial expressions are universal and the jaw drop is a distinct reaction linked to physiological arousal.
Physiological changes during emotional reactions include increased respiratory rate and muscle tension in the facial region.
